title: Literature Reviewing as an Architecture of Researchable Problems
abstract: A literature review is often taught as a preliminary collection of sources, yet its more important function is to construct a defensible research problem. This conceptual article reframes reviewing as an architecture of claims, relationships, and unresolved questions. It distinguishes six review purposes and proposes a workflow for delimiting the problem space, retrieving and evaluating evidence, coding claims, synthesizing relationships, and converting tensions into research questions.
